relationship_to_restored_text: Interpretive contemplative layer aligned by verse. This does not replace the source-audited restored translation.

verses.mystical_translation: Aaron's four sons open the priestly divisions.
Nadab and Abihu die before their father, and the surviving brothers carry the office.
David and two priestly leaders organize service.
Unequal household sizes produce sixteen and eight divisions.
Lots alternate between the two priestly branches.
A Levite scribe records the process before a broad public leadership group.
Jehoiarib and Jedaiah receive the first two appointments.
Harim and Seorim follow.
Malchijah and Mijamin follow.
Hakkoz and Abijah follow.
Jeshua and Shecaniah follow.
Eliashib and Jakim follow.
Huppah and Jeshebeab follow.
Bilgah and Immer follow.
Hezir and Happizzez follow.
Pethahiah and Jehezkel follow.
Jachin and Gamul follow.
Delaiah and Maaziah complete twenty-four courses.
The schedule becomes an inherited route into sanctuary service.
Remaining Levite houses begin with Shubael and Jehdeiah.
Isshiah leads Rehabiah's line.
Shelomoth and Jahath represent Izhar.
Hebron's four sons are named in order.
Micah and Shamir continue Uzziel's line.
Isshiah and Zechariah form another branch.
Merari, Mahli, Mushi, Jaaziah, and Beno enter the record.
Jaaziah's four sons continue the house.
Eleazar's childlessness is recorded without erasing him.
Jerahmeel continues Kish's line.
Mushi's sons complete the family list.
Chief and younger households receive corresponding lots before witnesses.

contemplative_note: Order can serve fairness when it is written, witnessed, and refuses seniority privilege. It becomes dangerous when inherited office is mistaken for inherited holiness. Lots and lineages can schedule work; they cannot replace consent, competence, accountability, or the equal spiritual dignity of those outside the roster.
